messages:
Dana Ruiz: Quick RFC follow-up: I want to propose a "signal mesh" approach for canary/A-B fallbacks. Core idea: evaluators publish typed, versioned signals into a mesh; actuators subscribe and apply a small deterministic policy DSL. Keeps actuators minimal and makes reasoning/audit easy.
Oliver Grant: Signal mesh sounds neat. How is it different from a central combiner?
Dana Ruiz: Mesh allows both central combiners and local combiners. Evaluators push signed signal packets; mesh routes them to local actuator agents for low-latency emergency heuristics and to central services for policy-level decisions and audit.
Priya Malhotra: Important: we need a canonical packet format. Suggest fields: channel, severity, score(0-100), rollout_id, cohort_pct, expires_at, provenance, evidence_link, seq_no. Packets must be signed and monotonic.
Ben Cho: For actuators, we should define a tiny policy DSL that's purely declarative: mapping rules like "when channel==latency AND score>70 AND cohort_pct<=5 then partial_divert:50% with ttl:120s". No imperative logic. That keeps actuators predictable.
Lena Moroz: Agree. Also add tokenized damping in DSL: each automatic action consumes a token; tokens refill per-policy. Prevents thrashing.
Dana Ruiz: On the local vs central combiner trade: local combiners handle critical short-circuit cases (e.g., GPU OOM spike) with high confidence and short ttl. Central combiner produces audited decisions that may override local within a short window and record to flight-recorder.
Oliver Grant: How do we handle irreversible ops like model swap? I fear local actuators shouldn't do those without central signed approval.
Priya Malhotra: Exactly. Define action categories: reversible (observe, partial_divert, quarantine_short) and irreversible (full_rollback, model_evict). Local actors may only execute reversible. Irreversible requires a signed central command with a staging window.
Ben Cho: For canary decay and cohort management: actuators should support fractional decay strategies: linear decay, multiplicative backoff, and evidence-driven shrink. DSL rule can specify the decay policy.
Lena Moroz: Auditability: flight-recorder must log raw signal packets, composed decision, applied action, and the policy rule id that triggered it. Keep retention 90d and provide quick links to evidence slices.
Dana Ruiz: Security: all packets signed with service keys; include seq_no + nonce to prevent replay. Mesh should validate signatures before handing to actuators.
Oliver Grant: Testing: we need a traffic replay harness that can feed synthetic noise and realistic metric skews. It should assert actuator stability properties (no more than N auto rollbacks in M minutes) and verify policy DSL correctness.
Priya Malhotra: Migration plan: start with shadow-mode only—actuator evaluates decisions but doesn't apply them. After 2 weeks of shadowing, enable reversible actions for low-risk services behind a feature flag. Finally allow irreversible ops with manual approval.
Ben Cho: Ops ergonomics: quick manual override via console + a per-rollout emergency kill-switch. Also expose recent applied actions with rollback buttons and links to the flight-recorder slice.
Lena Moroz: Edge case: multi-evaluator contention where one evaluator signals low confidence but many low-severity signals exist. We'll provide a combiner strategy param in the mesh: sum, max, weighted_avg, or custom plug-in. Central combiner populates "composed_score" and justification.
Dana Ruiz: Example packet (compact):
"""
packet:
  channel: latency
  severity: warn
  score: 78
  rollout_id: r-20260324-33
  cohort_pct: 5
  expires_at: 2026-03-24T13:02:00Z
  provenance: ["latency-eval-v2","sample-agg-east-1"]
  evidence_link: https://logs.example/service/1234
  seq_no: 98765
  signature: "<base64>"
"""
Oliver Grant: Nice. One more operational rule: actuators should enforce a min_dwell_seconds per-cohort and a cooldown multiplier after each auto-action to avoid flip-flop. DSL will expose those knobs.
Priya Malhotra: Ops safety budget: add policy keys like max_auto_rollbacks_per_day and cumulative_error_budget; once exhausted, mesh downgrades to manual-only and notifies owners.
Ben Cho: Implementation detail: prefer gRPC streaming for mesh with TLS + mTLS auth; fallback to signed HTTP for legacy agents. Use protobuf packet schema for compactness.
Lena Moroz: I'll prototype the DSL and a small interpreter for the actuator agent. We can keep the interpreter tiny and stateless; it just matches rules against validated packets.
rollout-bot: deploy: canary kicked off for content-suggester v1 cohort=4% at 2026-03-24T13:00Z :rocket:
Dana Ruiz: Great. Action items: Lena -> DSL prototype and interpreter, Oliver -> mesh validation and signature checks, Priya -> safety budget defaults, Ben -> decay strategies and test harness. We'll run a shadow pass for 2 weeks and then enable reversible actions for a handful of low-risk services.
